title: Eligible Organisations Encouraged to Apply for Recognition as Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) : Applications Open Till 31 August 2026
body_text:
51 GATCs already recognised | Verification scope expanded to 23 categories
More Verification Capacity • Faster Services • Better Consumer Protection
The Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, has invited online applications from eligible industries, laboratories, engineering colleges, polytechnics, ITIs and testing facilities for recognition as Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) under the Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013.
With the application window currently open, eligible organisations are encouraged to submit their applications through the Department's online portal emaap.gov.in/gatc before the deadline of 31 August 2026, up to 5:00 PM . The portal provides a completely digital process for submission of applications, payment of fees, tracking of application status and communication with applicants, making the process simpler, transparent and business-friendly.
The Department has earlier provided detailed information on the GATC framework, its expanded scope and the benefits of wider access to verification services.
Expanding verification capacity through wider participation
The GATC initiative is aimed at expanding India's verification ecosystem by enabling technically competent private sector institutions to participate in the verification and re-verification of specified weights and measures used in trade and commerce.
As on date, 51 GATCs have already been recognised. The Department is now further expanding the network so that businesses have greater access to verification facilities closer to their locations, reducing turnaround time and facilitating faster compliance.
The initiative will also complement the efforts of State Legal Metrology Departments. With more approved centres available for verification services, State Legal Metrology Officers can focus more on market surveillance, enforcement and consumer grievance redressal.
23 categories of weights and measures now covered
Following recent amendments to the GATC Rules, recognised GATCs can undertake verification and re-verification of 23 categories of weights and measures covering important sectors such as healthcare, energy, transport, retail, manufacturing and infrastructure. These include:
(i) Water meters
(ii) Sphygmomanometers
(iii) Clinical thermometers
(iv) Automatic rail weighbridges
(v) Tape measures
(vi) Non-automatic weighing instruments of Accuracy Class III (up to 150 kg)
(vii) Non-automatic weighing instruments of Accuracy Class IIII
(viii) Load cells
(ix) Beam scales
(x) Counter machines
(xi) Weights of all categories
(xii) Gas meters
(xiii) Energy meters
(xiv) Moisture meters
(xv) Vehicle speed meters
(xvi) Breath analysers
(xvii) Multi-dimensional measuring instruments
(xviii) Flow meters
(xix) Petrol and diesel dispensers
(xx) CNG dispensers
(xxi) LPG dispensers
(xxii) LNG dispensers
(xxiii) Hydrogen dispensers.
The inclusion of petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG, LNG and hydrogen dispensers is part of the recent expansion of the GATC framework. This will help strengthen verification capacity for fuel dispensing systems and support accurate measurement and transparency in fuel transactions.
A simpler route for industry
The expansion of GATCs is an important Ease of Doing Business reform. Instead of relying only on limited departmental facilities for verification, manufacturers, traders and users can increasingly access approved technical facilities through the expanding GATC network.
The digital application system further simplifies the process by enabling applicants to apply online, make payments digitally and track their applications without the need for repeated physical visits to Government offices.
Eligible organisations are required to have the prescribed testing and calibration equipment traceable to national standards, qualified technical personnel and the infrastructure specified under the GATC Rules.
Partnership for stronger legal metrology services
The GATC framework represents a partnership approach in Legal Metrology. By bringing technically capable laboratories, industries, educational and testing institutions into the verification ecosystem, the Government is increasing the availability of reliable verification services while maintaining the regulatory oversight prescribed under the Legal Metrology framework.
This approach will help create a larger, more accessible and responsive verification network, benefiting both businesses and consumers.
Faster compliance, reliable measurements and consumer protection
Accurate weights and measures are essential for fair transactions and consumer confidence. A wider network of GATCs will help make verification and re-verification services more accessible and timely, thereby supporting businesses in meeting their regulatory requirements while ensuring that measurements used in commercial transactions remain accurate and reliable.
The reform therefore seeks to achieve a balance between Ease of Doing Business and consumer protection, making compliance easier for honest businesses while strengthening confidence in measurements used in everyday transactions.
The Department's GATC reforms are also aligned with its broader efforts towards digital governance, Atmanirbhar Bharat and strengthening India's quality infrastructure, including alignment with internationally accepted measurement practices.
Applications remain open till 31 August 2026
Eligible organisations interested in becoming Government Approved Test Centres may submit their applications online through emaap.gov.in/gatc .
Application period: 17 August 2026 to 31 August 2026
Last date/time: 31 August 2026, up to 5:00 PM
Detailed eligibility conditions, prescribed requirements and the application process are available on the portal. Eligible organisations are encouraged to complete the application process before the deadline. With 51 GATCs already recognised and the verification scope expanded to 23 categories, the Department is further widening India's measurement verification network to provide industry with easier access to services, faster compliance and consumers with greater confidence in the accuracy of commercial measurements.

RT/SB/ARC

ministry.name: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

enrichment.summary: The Department of Consumer Affairs has invited online applications (till 31 August 2026, 5:00 PM) from eligible industries, laboratories, engineering colleges, polytechnics, ITIs and testing facilities to be recognised as Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) under the Legal Metrology (GATC) Rules, 2013. Currently 51 GATCs are recognised, and following recent rule amendments the scope of verification has been expanded to 23 categories of weights and measures, including newly added fuel dispensers (petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG, LNG, hydrogen). Applications are submitted through the digital portal emaap.gov.in/gatc, which handles submission, fee payment and status tracking.
enrichment.context:
Legal Metrology in India regulates weights and measures used in trade and commerce to ensure accuracy and consumer protection, administered under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 and associated rules. Traditionally, verification and re-verification of weighing and measuring instruments was carried out largely through government-run facilities, which often faced capacity constraints and delays. The GATC scheme, introduced under the Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013, allows technically competent private and institutional laboratories to be authorised to perform these verification functions, thereby expanding capacity without diluting regulatory oversight by State Legal Metrology Departments.

This release reflects an incremental administrative update — a routine call for applications — but it carries some substantive policy content: the expansion of verifiable categories to 23, notably including fuel dispensers (petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG, LNG, hydrogen), which is relevant given India's push for accurate fuel metering and transparency amid growing alternative fuel infrastructure. It also fits within the government's broader Ease of Doing Business agenda and digital governance push (via the emaap.gov.in portal), aligning with themes like Atmanirbhar Bharat and quality infrastructure development.

prelims_questions.question: Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) in India are recognised under which of the following?
options: The Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013
The Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016
prelims_questions.explanation: GATCs are recognised under the Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013, which allow eligible private and institutional laboratories to undertake verification and re-verification of weights and measures.

prelims_questions.question: As per the recent expansion of the GATC framework, which of the following categories of weights and measures has been newly brought under GATC verification scope?
options: Only water meters and gas meters
Only weighing instruments used in retail
Fuel dispensers including petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG, LNG and hydrogen dispensers
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that recent amendments to the GATC Rules expanded coverage to 23 categories, including the newly added petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG, LNG and hydrogen dispensers, to strengthen verification of fuel dispensing systems.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Government Approved Test Centre (GATC) scheme in strengthening India's legal metrology framework. How does such a public-private partnership model balance Ease of Doing Business with consumer protection?

Accurate weights and measures are essential for consumer confidence and fair trade. Examine the challenges in India's legal metrology verification ecosystem and suggest reforms to enhance its efficiency and reach.

study_notes.reason: The release is primarily a factual/administrative update on the GATC scheme under the Legal Metrology Act — the legal basis, number of centres, and expanded categories are testable facts, while the analytical content (ease of doing business, decentralisation of verification) is thin and largely rhetorical.

prelims.point: Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) are recognised under the Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013, framed under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.
prelims.why_important: UPSC could test the parent Act and year of the GATC Rules as a factual link in Legal Metrology governance.

prelims.point: Verification scope of GATCs has been expanded to 23 categories of weights and measures, newly including fuel dispensers (petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG, LNG, hydrogen).
prelims.why_important: The inclusion of hydrogen and LNG dispensers signals alignment with alternative fuel infrastructure, a distinctive and testable detail.

prelims.point: Nodal authority: Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution administers the Legal Metrology framework, while enforcement rests with State Legal Metrology Departments.
prelims.why_important: Tests the distinction between central rule-making/recognition and state-level enforcement in Legal Metrology governance.

mains.point: The GATC scheme exemplifies a public-private partnership model to expand regulatory verification capacity without diluting oversight, freeing State Legal Metrology Officers to focus on market surveillance and enforcement.
mains.theme: Regulatory capacity building via private participation
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on innovative governance models that expand public service delivery through accredited private/institutional participation while retaining regulatory control.

mains.point: Expansion of verifiable categories to fuel dispensers, including hydrogen and LNG, reflects the need to update regulatory frameworks in step with emerging alternative fuel infrastructure.
mains.analytical_use: Can be used in answers on aligning consumer protection and metrology regulation with India's energy transition and fuel diversification goals.
